verdict.rationale: Keycloak is a standards-based OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect authorization server. You register clients, including through a dynamic client registration endpoint, and it exposes a well-known discovery endpoint plus introspection and revocation endpoints. It supports client-credentials and device grants, and themes let the login carry your app's branding. Together these let a developer stand up a "Sign in with my app" provider that issues tokens to third-party clients. The main caveat is that Keycloak runs as a separate server in front of your app, not inside it; your existing user store can be connected through a custom user-federation provider. Missing for 10: evidence of a third-party consent/authorization screen and per-client scope consent, and independent hands-on corroboration of exposing Keycloak to external third-party developers.
